transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Arbor Tech, Head of AI), Tom Reed (Arbor Tech, Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Arbor Tech, Security Lead)

Summary (auto): quick midweek check to validate recent drift, review scorecard spike, and align on a rollback drill next week.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, quick roll call. we got ethan from our se team.
[00:18] Ethan Park: hi all, morning — afternoon — depending where you are. got the experiment results loaded.
[00:27] Sofia Alvarez: thanks, Maya. we saw the scorecard jump tuesday night so wanted to understand root cause and rollback options.
[00:36] Tom Reed: yeah, the failure mode looked like hallucination in the product-summary path — a few short docs triggered spurious completions.
[00:45] Maya Chen: okay, good callout. ethan can you walk through the runs you did? and, um, any trans codes or hmm misreads in the kv cache we should watch for?
[00:58] Ethan Park: sure; so i re-ran the batch from monday and then replayed the 1k failure set. we saw latency stable but precision dropped on the named-entity extraction prompts. sequence: prompt-set B shows +12% false positives versus baseline A. quick caveat: the transcript engine used here munged some tokens — the KV came out as K V cash in the logs, so when you look at raw logs please forgive OCR-like errors.
[01:25] Sofia Alvarez: when you say false positives can you give an example — we saw product names getting collapsed into category names.
[01:34] Ethan Park: yeah an example: input snippet about "MapleGuard 2.0" was summarized as "mapleguard products" and that triggered a downstream tagger to assign wrong SKUs. scoring on the test harness: baseline F1 was 0.82, current drop to 0.71 on that slice.
[01:52] Tom Reed: do we know whether this is model drift, prompt drift, or dataset mismatch? we updated the scraper last week so could be input distribution shift.
[02:03] Maya Chen: good question. ethan?
[02:06] Ethan Park: early signal points to prompt/context mismatch — some new docs are longer, pushing past the prefix cache behavior and kv-cache reuse. runtime chose a different kernel path for 2 long sequences which changed tokenization slightly. that plus prompt-set B's liberal temperature for diversity increased hallucinations.
[02:28] Priya Singh: from security side we want to ensure any rollback doesn't leak data or temporarily disable auditing. what's the plan for preserving audit logs during a canary rollback?
[02:38] Ethan Park: by default we keep audit logs in the control plane; for private deploys we can stream to your S3 and retain immutable copies. for the rollback drill we propose keep-audit=true and snapshot the keystore access logs.
[02:55] Maya Chen: note: priya asked for snapshotting KMS events and the policy — can you confirm that, priya?
[03:02] Priya Singh: yes, we need KMS key rotation window and whether Redwood needs write access to the key metadata. also, does the host use customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed?
[03:13] Ethan Park: in your current pilot you set customer-managed KMS, so we don't hold the plaintext. we only call via enclave with enveloped keys. we'll export the key policy example in the next email.
[03:25] Sofia Alvarez: perfect. on the scoring side we also noticed a sensitivity to the prompt temperature change — is it feasible to pin temperature for canary and then open it for production?
[03:34] Ethan Park: yes. we can pin a config: rollout env variable that sets temperature and top_p per route. for canary we recommend conservative temp 0.0-0.2.
[03:44] Tom Reed: about the 5k run you mentioned in the invite, what env will that be on — dedicated or hosted? how close to prod?
[03:52] Maya Chen: we'll run it on a dedicated pool to emulate latency and batching. ethan, can you describe differences customers should expect between dedicated and hosted results?
[04:03] Ethan Park: dedicated gives predictable throughput and the same model binary but with different batching heuristics; small variance in tail latency depending on queue depth. hosted sometimes coalesces more aggressively but we won't do that for your canary. cost per-token will be slightly higher on dedicated with smaller batch sizes, but latency becomes more consistent.
[04:23] Sofia Alvarez: what's the expected token cost for 5k samples? quick ballpark.
[04:27] Ethan Park: from the preliminary run: roughly 1.8M tokens total, cost ~ $120-150 depending on quantization settings. i'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:35] Priya Singh: can we get an export of the per-token breakdown tied to user ids for audit?
[04:41] Ethan Park: yes we can generate token-level traces, redacted except for request metadata. we'll hash user ids or use pseudonyms if needed.
[04:48] Maya Chen: jumping back to regression: did you try prompt-surgery (reduce context, strip templates) to see if that recovers baseline?
[04:57] Ethan Park: i did a quick A/B: trimmed context to 512 tokens and enforced stricter system prompt. results: false positives drop to +3% above baseline — so partial recovery. long-doc cases still fail.
[05:12] Sofia Alvarez: so it sounds like two parallel workstreams: short-term guardrail tweaks and long-term ingestion changes.
[05:18] Tom Reed: yep. for ingestion we can add a preprocessor to chunk and annotate documents before they hit the model. cost/time to implement that?
[05:27] Tom Reed: estimated 3 engineer-days to land a preprocessor that chunk/summarize.
[05:31] Maya Chen: can we do a workaround using automatic chunking in the runtime versus engineering effort on your side?
[05:36] Ethan Park: runtime-level prefix-splitting is possible; we can enable auto-chunking in the serving layer and preserve prefix cache semantics. tradeoff: added per-request overhead and potential higher token costs.
[05:50] Priya Singh: whatever we do we need to keep logs for compliance. also, will enabling auto-chunking change our model signature or impact SSO tokens?
[05:59] Ethan Park: no change to SSO. model signature is same; we may add an extra header in the request to indicate chunking metadata.
[06:07] Sofia Alvarez: can we talk guardrails — what exactly would you change? thresholds, reject rules?
[06:12] Ethan Park: propose three levers: 1) tighten scoring threshold for tagger (reject if confidence < 0.7), 2) add post-generation regex filters for SKU patterns, 3) enable a fallback to a smaller deterministic model for high-risk routes.
[06:27] Tom Reed: fallback sounds interesting — latency/ cost tradeoffs?
[06:31] Ethan Park: fallback model is cheaper but slightly less fluent. cost savings maybe 40% on those requests; latency is similar if we pre-warm the pool.
[06:39] Maya Chen: for the canary rollback drill, what are the exact steps? can we outline now?
[06:44] Ethan Park: rough rollback runbook: 1) cut traffic to canary 10% -> monitor scorecard 15 min, 2) if metric spike, switch to fallback model + enable stricter threshold, 3) if critical, route traffic to pre-rollback snapshot (pin model version) and trigger ops page. we'll share a runbook doc.
[07:03] Sofia Alvarez: who drives the page? you or us?
[07:06] Maya Chen: AE will coordinate but platform on-call should own the page. tom, priya — would you like to own the page?
[07:14] Tom Reed: we can own it, yes. we'll need a contact from your side for escalation.
[07:18] Maya Chen: i'll be the escalation lead; ethan will be primary SE.
[07:22] Priya Singh: related to compliance, does redwood support tenant-level retention policies so we can purge tokens older than X?
[07:30] Ethan Park: yes — retention is configurable per-tenant. for your account we can enable 90-day retention or custom retention and run a one-time purge for training data.
[07:40] Sofia Alvarez: great. on the scoring front, can you share the diff between prompt-set A and B? we want to see exactly what changed.
[07:47] Ethan Park: i'll attach the prompt diff in the email and include the guardrail config export — i noticed prompt B added an "examples" block which increases creative completions.
[07:57] Tom Reed: small note — our downstream tagger treats punctuation differently; some of the hallucination may be due to punctuation collapse during tokenization.
[08:05] Ethan Park: good catch. i'll add a tokenization normalization step in the preprocessor suggestions.
[08:12] Maya Chen: let's tighten the action list. ethan you'll run the 5k on dedicated and share the latency/cost sheet by 7/15.
[08:20] Ethan Park: noted.
[08:22] Maya Chen: sofia you will upload the 200 edge-case examples by 7/13 so we can run targeted tests.
[08:28] Sofia Alvarez: yes.
[08:29] Maya Chen: priya will confirm KMS constraints and SOC2 window by 7/14.
[08:33] Priya Singh: will do.
[08:34] Tom Reed: i'll schedule the canary roll drill internal invite and ensure on-call coverage.
[08:38] Maya Chen: thanks. a couple of clarifications — do we want a hard rollback to previous model version or a staged fallback?
[08:46] Sofia Alvarez: staged fallback preferred so customers don't see blackouts.
[08:50] Ethan Park: agree. staged fallback with stricter thresholds first, then hard rollback only if escalation.
[08:57] Maya Chen: ok noted. any blockers on your side to proceed?
[09:01] Sofia Alvarez: only that we need the token cost spreadsheet for budget approval this week.
[09:06] Ethan Park: i'll prioritize that; expect an email by end of day tomorrow with the first pass.
[09:12] Maya Chen: will you also include quantization options? customer asked about 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs.
[09:18] Ethan Park: yes i'll include quantization impacts on latency/cost/accuracy. initial notes: 8-bit gives near-same accuracy; 4-bit shows slight drop in NER cases.
[09:30] Priya Singh: last compliance Q: when we run the 5k, can we limit PII exposure in logs?
[09:36] Ethan Park: yes we can hash PII in transit and redact from logs; we'll provide the redaction policy.
[09:41] Maya Chen: great. any other questions?
[09:44] Tom Reed: none from me.
[09:46] Sofia Alvarez: quick ask: add a column in the results for "reason code" for failed samples so we can triage by failure mode.
[09:54] Ethan Park: will do.
[09:55] Maya Chen: okay, wrapping — recap: 5k run, edge-case upload, KMS confirmation, runbook for canary, prompt diff and guardrail export.
[10:06] Sofia Alvarez: thumbs up.
[10:07] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and docs.
[10:12] (call ends)

Notes / Links mentioned:
- Shared results spreadsheet (to be attached): https://redwood.app/poc/arbor-tech/5k-results
- Prompt diff and guardrail export: will be shared via email
- Customer edge labels path: /arbor/poc/edge_labels.csv (customer-side)

Questions (auto):
- Can Redwood run 5k on dedicated pool that simulates production? -> Yes, SE to run and share numbers.
- Will audit logs be preserved during rollback? -> Yes, snapshot and stream to customer S3.

Action items (repeated):
- Ethan Park — run 5k and share latency/cost sheet (due 2026-07-15)
- Sofia Alvarez — upload 200 edge-case labels (due 2026-07-13)
- Priya Singh — confirm KMS policy and SOC2 window (due 2026-07-14)
- Maya Chen — draft canary rollback runbook and send invite (due 2026-07-10)

End of transcript.
